svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-expertise-newsletter-operating-functions; chapter number: 11; title: Build the Newsletter Around a Reader Problem; subtitle: Connect positioning, repeatable publishing, suitable advertising, and outcome-led offers.; caption: Nicolas Cole emphasizes positioning and discovery; beehiiv demonstrates repeatable production and advertising operations; Write • Build • Scale develops reader conversations; Matt McGarry connects cohort assignments to promised outcomes.; assumptions note: Nicolas Cole, beehiiv, Write • Build • Scale, and Matt McGarry describe operating practices, not a shared staffing structure. The functions do not imply separate employees, and publisher headcount is not specified.; note: beehiiv reports up to five claimed advertising offers at once and five days to publish. Stack Receipts advises comparing advertising earnings with the plan bill at the same list size and billing cadence.; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Expertise-led newsletter publisher; headcount: Not specified; focus: Serve a specific reader problem with a repeatable publication and relevant paid outcomes, following Nicolas Cole and Write • Build • Scale.; spokes: role: Positioning and discovery; type: Audience-development function; kpi: Reader acquisition by source; Nicolas Cole reports over 50% of Write With AI's acquisition came from inside Substack's ecosystem.; role: Repeatable issue production; type: Editorial function; kpi: A repeatable issue format and publishing routine; beehiiv's Dope Act example saves the drafting process as a Claude skill.; role: Advertising operations; type: Placement and reporting function; kpi: Suitable placements within beehiiv's reported five-day claim window; reject unsuitable offers with a reason.; role: Reader outcomes and paid offers; type: Product and learning function; kpi: Assignments sufficient for the promised outcome, as Matt McGarry requires; use reader conversations about goals and obstacles as Write • Build • Scale recommends.
